key_insight: Text-level safety and physically grounded danger are separable in LLM hidden states, so a model can look linguistically safe while still encoding unsafe action risk.
engineering_relevance: For embodied agents and tool-using LLMs, hidden-state risk probing offers a lighter-weight safety layer than prompt-only moderation or judge models, reducing false blocks on safe tasks.
method: Analyzed hidden-state directions to test whether content danger (CD) and physical danger (PD) occupy different representation spaces.
Built PRISM, a single-layer L2-regularized logistic probe over full hidden states.
Validated the probe with random-split null tests and cross-benchmark replication.
evidence_signal: Across Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B/32B, Phi-3.5, and SmolLM2, PRISM achieved 86.2–87.7% accuracy on SafeAgentBench and 99.6% on PSB-1K, while LLM judges showed much higher false-positive rates on safe tasks.
watch_item: Because PRISM is a representation-level classifier, it may depend on model-specific hidden states and require careful calibration when transferred to new architectures or domains.
paper_title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
